CNC milling
CNC milling for custom components

Custom milling for housings and other components with pockets, bores and detailed profiles. Send your drawing to discuss the machining requirements.

Prepare RFQ email
Multi-bore circular milled component
Milled pockets, faces and contours

An instrument housing or bracket may need features machined from several directions. The model determines the stock form, tool access and setup sequence.

Geometry & process
For pockets, slots, flat faces and features cut from several directions. 3-, 4- and 5-axis work covers brackets, manifolds, multi-sided parts and curved surfaces.
Size & workholding
Send a 3D model with the overall dimensions and stock size. Setup planning considers tool access, clamping space and the relationships between features. Axis count alone does not determine the maximum part size.
Materials
Aluminum, stainless steel, steel, copper, brass, titanium and engineering plastics. Confirm the grade and stock condition on your drawing.
Finishes
Deburring, polishing, bead blasting, anodizing and plating. Options depend on the substrate and the dimensions that need protection; specify the finish on your drawing.

Drawing & acceptance
Drawing requirements

Identify the assembly datums and dimensions that locate mating bores, mounting holes and faces. Separate functional dimensions from general dimensions.

Mark deep pockets and small internal corners, along with thin sections that need tool-access or workholding checks. State where a radius or geometry change is acceptable.

Inspection and acceptance

Identify which face, bore and hole-position relationships need recorded results, and the datum system used to evaluate them.

Specify whether dimensional acceptance applies before or after finishing, with masking and cosmetic surfaces marked on the drawing.

Agree the measurement method and required records before production.

±0.01 mm — Evaluated critical-feature reference. Selected critical features may be evaluated against this reference after engineering review. Material, geometry, setup and measurement method affect feasibility. It is not a default or guaranteed tolerance.

Quality & inspection
Equipment and order records
Prepare your milling enquiry

Supply a 3D model and revision-controlled drawing, material grade and stock condition, quantity and intended assembly.

Include finish requirements and any permitted design changes so alternative machining approaches can be evaluated.

Prepare RFQ email

Add your requirements to the email draft, then attach drawings in your email app before sending.
